identity.title: Taming Momentum: Rethinking Optimizer States Through Low-Rank Approximation

problem.claim: Large-model optimizers such as Adam and Muon incur substantial memory overhead from first- and second-order momentum states, limiting scalability and computational efficiency.

contributions.claim: Reframes EMA momentum as online gradient-flow training of a linear regressor and introduces LoRA-Pre, a low-rank optimizer for efficient pre-training.
Decomposes the full momentum matrix into a compact low-rank subspace to reduce optimizer memory while aiming to maintain optimization performance.
Evaluates LoRA-Pre in both pre-training and fine-tuning settings across Llama-family models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe LoRA-Pre as a novel low-rank optimizer derived from the EMA–online-linear-learner equivalence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report highest performance across all tested model sizes when pre-training Llama-family models from 60M to 1B parameters.
The authors report comparable or superior results using one-eighth the rank of baseline methods.

In fine-tuning, the authors report that LoRA-Pre with the same rank consistently outperforms efficient fine-tuning baselines, including gains of 3.14 points on Llama-3.1-8B and 6.17 points on Llama-2-7B versus standard LoRA.

narrative_sequence.summary: Optimizer momentum states create memory overhead that constrains large-model training.
EMA momentum is recast as online gradient-flow training of a linear regressor.
LoRA-Pre applies a compact low-rank decomposition to momentum states for memory-efficient pre-training.
The method is reported to perform strongly in Llama-family pre-training and fine-tuning, including rank efficiency and improvements over baselines.
The authors provide a public code repository.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a conceptual equivalence between EMA and online linear learning directly to the design of a low-rank optimizer.

lessons.interpretation: A mechanistic reframing can supply a clear bridge from optimizer-state structure to a concrete memory-saving design.
lessons.application: When proposing a state-compression method, first identify an equivalent learning process whose structure motivates the compression.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the claimed equivalence does not preserve the optimization behavior relevant to the target setting.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports both scale coverage and rank-matched comparisons, including a one-eighth-rank result and fine-tuning gains against standard LoRA.

lessons.interpretation: Reporting resource efficiency alongside task performance makes the practical tradeoff more explicit.
lessons.application: Pair performance comparisons with matched-budget or compressed-resource comparisons and state the relevant scale.
lessons.exception: A rank- or budget-matched comparison is insufficient when methods differ materially in other training conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation metric, baseline identities beyond standard LoRA, statistical variability, or detailed training conditions.
The meaning of “highest performance,” “comparable,” and “substantial improvements” is not operationally defined.
The abstract does not quantify absolute memory savings or establish whether the reported results generalize beyond the tested Llama-family settings.
